remarks_1999: I could send one that is four feet by seven — it is that yellow streak you returned to me done over as a horizontal — the color much brighter [see cat. no. 1262] — and Im doing it again now four feet by six and the color is just plain color out of the tube — red and orange to lemon — It shocks me so that Im rather struck with it — I don't know what it will get to (O'Keeffe to Edith Halpert, 8 August 1954, Archive of American Art). "The second painting 'From the Plains' [cat. no. 1262] is at the Kecks. I sent it to have a rubbed place spotted and to have it sprayed" (O'Keeffe to Edith Halpert, 13 August 1958, Archive of American Art). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: From the Plains II

description: A bright yellow, lightning bolt-like shape arches over an expanse of orange paint. Along the canvas' bottom edge is a strip of vibrant red paint.  Another smaller lightning bolt of yellow zigzags near the bottom right corner of the work.
title: From the Plains II
